name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3478
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: Composer taking and retaking ingredients of Advil? Not!

indicators.note: the ingredients of a recipe are used in any order, so the letters are freely recombined

blocks.note: the brand name of a painkiller followed by a flat denial, taken letter by letter
retaking lets some of the same letters be used a second time

explanation.surface: A musician keeps reaching for the components of a headache pill, then insists it is not that at all.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: ANTONIO VIVALDI uses only the eight letters of ADVIL NOT, some of them more than once, which is what 'taking and retaking' allows.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of the violin concertos known collectively as The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Rethink thorniest achievements in baseball

indicators.note: rethinking something reworks it, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reconsidering the most difficult feats in the game of baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hitter is a baseball game in which a pitcher allows the opposing team no hits, a celebrated feat.

clue.text: Undisciplined son keeps dependent ahead

indicators.note: undisciplined letters are unruly and will not stay in their given order
keeps means the jumbled letters hold another word inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
a ward is a minor in someone's legal care, a dependent

explanation.surface: An unruly boy keeps his young charge out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward, in a direction ahead of where one is.

clue.text: Spiritual banquet starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the opening letter is missed out

blocks.note: a dinner can be a formal banquet

explanation.surface: A religious feast that begins behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner refers to the mind or soul, as in inner life, so it can mean spiritual.

clue.text: Wives' largely liberal opinion

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
liberal means free, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The progressive outlook held by most married women.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or opinion someone holds.

clue.text: Competes to eat egg, potatoes, carrots, and so on

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the competing word swallows another

blocks.note: to vie is to compete
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating contests involving eggs, spuds and carrots.
explanation.definitionFit: Veggies is an informal word for vegetables, of which potatoes and carrots are examples.

clue.text: Moving top to bottom of smooth 6

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is moved round to the end

blocks.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: Shifting the lid of a polished set of vegetables to the base.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 6 down, VEGGIES; a cross-reference number stands in for that answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeks are onion-family plants eaten as vegetables, so they are examples of veggies.

clue.text: In Glasgow, John Irving adapted novelist's introductions

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A Scottish fan of a famous American novelist reworks his books.
explanation.walkthrough: John Irving is the novelist of The World According to Garp, which makes 'adapted' look like a film adaptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian is the Scottish form of the given name John, so a Glaswegian John is an Ian.

clue.text: Corrected, I call a UFO sighting originally wrong

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word for a viewing
corrected text has been fixed, so the letters are fixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of sighting

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to having mistaken something for a flying saucer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also hides FALL, one of the seasons in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallacious means based on a mistaken belief or unsound reasoning, so it means wrong.

clue.text: What remains after a fire: a tree

blocks.note: first meaning: the powdery residue left by burning
second meaning: a deciduous hardwood tree of the olive family

explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes the tree sound like the thing that burned, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the grey residue left by combustion and a common hardwood tree used for tool handles.

clue.text: Herb's terrible regret: getting involved in white nationalism at first

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order
getting involved in something means going inside it, so the jumbled letters go within the drink
at first points to the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: a white is a glass of white wine
taken as written
the first letter of nationalism

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb bitterly regrets having been drawn into white nationalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white nationalism' reads as one political phrase; split it, and white is the drink while nationalism gives only its first letter. The answer hides WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is an aromatic evergreen plant whose leaves yield a minty oil used as a flavouring herb.

clue.text: Bookish queen loses head after a certain amount of drink

indicators.note: losing its head means the royal name gives up its opening letter
after places the beheaded name behind the measure of drink rather than in front

blocks.note: a metric measure of liquid, in the American spelling
a queen's name, as in Mary Queen of Scots

explanation.surface: A well-read monarch is decapitated after downing a measured quantity of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: LITER is the American spelling of litre, natural in this US puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes a person fond of books and learning, a close synonym of bookish.

clue.text: Puzzle dances? That's so cute!

blocks.note: a jig is a lively folk dance
the cooing exclamation people make at something adorable

explanation.surface: Someone watching little dancers being puzzled and then melting at how sweet they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces that you fit back together.

clue.text: Ida, a renowned journalist and snob, retaining name as a source

indicators.note: retaining means the word for a snob holds another letter inside it

blocks.note: Ida B. Wells, the American investigative journalist and civil rights campaigner
a prig is a self-righteous, superior person
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A celebrated reporter who looks down on people still keeps her byline as a source of stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Ida B. Wells was a pioneering African American journalist who exposed lynching in the 1890s. The answer hides SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is the head of a spring, and figuratively an abundant source of anything.

clue.text: Song of unprotected outcast

indicators.note: without its protective covering, the word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: a pariah is a social outcast

explanation.surface: A lament sung by a vulnerable exile.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song for a voice in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Considers violating vows in good humor

indicators.note: violating something breaks it, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for good humour

blocks.note: cheer is a cheerful, good-humoured mood
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about breaking their promises, and does so cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew over is an idiom for thinking something through at length, so it means considers.

clue.text: Swap backs of enormous containers

indicators.note: swapping the back letters means only the last two trade places

blocks.note: vast means enormous

explanation.surface: Exchanging the rear parts of gigantic storage bins.
explanation.definitionFit: Vats are large tanks or tubs for holding liquids, so they are containers.

clue.text: Gets booty back in seat

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for grabbing plunder from right to left

blocks.note: to loot is to seize plunder

explanation.surface: Sounds like a pirate taking treasure back to where he sits, or a pun on booty as the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple backless seat for one person.

clue.text: Start to obtain tattered futon covering to haul away

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
tattered fabric is torn apart, so the letters are pulled out of order
covering means the jumbled letters go around the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of obtain
taken as written
to tow is to haul a vehicle along

explanation.surface: Getting a ragged mattress hauled off to the dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haul away' reads as one phrase, but 'to haul' is the wordplay and 'away' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of town means away from home, travelling elsewhere.

clue.text: Where you might find actors in the beginning

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: performers are on the film set
second meaning: the start of something

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as two words for the actors, run it together for the start of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is the start or commencement of something, especially an illness or season, so it equals beginning.

clue.text: Storm furiously at donor

indicators.note: something done furiously is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone raging angrily at a person who gave money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' reads as a verb, rage at; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, one kind of storm.

clue.text: They make up your side with repeated helpings of meats

indicators.note: two servings dished out in different arrangements, so the same letters appear twice, each time reordered

blocks.note: the first helping, without its plural ending
the repeated helping, all five letters

explanation.surface: A dinner where your side of the table is filled up by second portions of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves are each rearrangements of the same food word: one of four letters, one with the plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: Teammates are fellow members of a team, the people who together form your side in a game.

clue.text: Mother incoherently rants watchwords

indicators.note: incoherent words make no sense in that order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother babbling her favourite slogans.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantras are slogans or phrases repeated often, much like watchwords or mottoes.

clue.text: Stern veers east unexpectedly

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly departs from its usual course, so the letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A ship's back end swings round to the east without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like the back of the boat in this nautical surface, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and stern are synonyms describing a strict, harsh, unsmiling manner.

clue.text: No backing for Williams at empty stadium

indicators.note: having no back means the final letter of the tennis name is removed

blocks.note: Venus Williams, the American tennis champion
E marks empty on a fuel gauge

explanation.surface: A tennis star gets no support from a crowd in a deserted arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is a place where events such as games are held, and a stadium is one.

clue.text: Represent California university's shifting defense

indicators.note: shifting moves things about, so the letters of the college name are moved into a new order

blocks.note: Stanford University is in California
surface padding: completes the football picture and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: Playing for a Californian college whose football defence keeps changing formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defense' finishes the sporting picture; the letters come only from the university's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for something is to symbolise or represent it, as initials stand for a name.

clue.text: British politician wearing shirt in Arizona city

indicators.note: a person wearing clothing is inside it, so these letters go within the garment

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A British lawmaker in a T-shirt visiting the American Southwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempe is a city in Arizona near Phoenix, home of Arizona State University.

clue.text: Pronounced drain for plaintiff

indicators.note: pronounced means we go by how the word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a sewer is an underground drain

explanation.surface: A distinct drain set aside for someone bringing a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suer is one who sues, and a plaintiff is the party bringing a case to court.

clue.text: '70s singer is a total mess, initially interrupting party

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word for a muddle
something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another thing, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the Donner Party, the ill-fated American pioneer group of 1846
taken as written
a sum is a total
the first letter of mess

explanation.surface: A disco-era star is in a complete state, starting to wreck a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Donner Party were pioneers snowbound in the Sierra Nevada in 1846, which makes 'party' a sly name rather than a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna Summer was the American disco singer of the 1970s known for hits like I Feel Love.

clue.text: Note time period

blocks.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Jotting down a length of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' looks like a span of time; it is the American name for a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a period is the punctuation mark, which is a small dot.

clue.text: Admit cutting the front off dress

indicators.note: cutting off the front removes the opening letter of the garment word

blocks.note: a gown is a long dress

explanation.surface: Confessing to having snipped the front off a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up or own a fault is to acknowledge or confess it, so own means admit.

clue.text: Safe and honest combination holding what belongs to us for a whole year — they can be found in the completed diagram

definitions.text: they can be found in the completed diagram

indicators.note: a combination is a mix of things, so these letters are mixed together
holding means the mixed letters wrap around the possessive word

blocks.note: taken as written, the and joining the two words
the possessive pronoun for something of ours

explanation.surface: A combination lock on a safe, guarding our belongings all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid hides all four: WINTER in 11, SPRING in 14, SUMMER in 29 and FALL in 9, matching Vivaldi in 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The four seasons together make up a whole year, and each one is hidden inside another answer here.
